records.source: וַתִּקְרַ֜בְנָה בְּנ֣וֹת צְלָפְחָ֗ד בֶּן־חֵ֤פֶר בֶּן־גִּלְעָד֙ בֶּן־מָכִ֣יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לְמִשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בֶן־יוֹסֵ֑ף וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ שְׁמ֣וֹת בְּנֹתָ֔יו מַחְלָ֣ה נֹעָ֔ה וְחָגְלָ֥ה וּמִלְכָּ֖ה וְתִרְצָֽה׃
records.gloss: And drew near [the] daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, of [the] clans of Manasseh son of Joseph; and these [are the] names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
pieces: Then the daughters of Zelophehad came forward. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, and belonged to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. His daughters were named Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

L.1: And the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph, drew near; and these [are the] names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.

R.1: Zelophehad had five daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah. Their family came from the tribe of Manasseh, the son of Joseph. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, and Hepher was a descendant of Gilead, Machir and Manasseh. One day his daughters came forward with a request.

decisions.choice: Zelophehad and his daughters: the family named in the census of chapter 26
decisions.reason: The census just taken lists Zelophehad son of Hepher of the clan of Manasseh as a man who had daughters and no sons, and names these five women (26:33). The land was to be shared out by the names counted in that census (26:52-56), so the daughters now ask what will happen to their father's share. Their case returns in 36:1-12 and Joshua 17:3-6.

decisions.choice: drew near: came forward to present a case
decisions.reason: The verb means to come near or approach. Here it is the formal step of coming before the leaders to put a matter to them, as the next verse describes.

decisions.choice: of the clans of Manasseh: their place in the tribe that the land is shared by
decisions.reason: The family line is traced back six generations to Joseph. Land in Israel was held by tribe, clan and family, so a person's line decided where his share of the land would be.

decisions.choice: names first, then the family line
decisions.reason: Readable gives the five names first and the long family line after it in short sentences, so young readers can follow who is meant. It adds "with a request" to lead into verses 2-4, which say what they asked.

records.heading: The daughters of Zelophehad

records.source: וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֜דְנָה לִפְנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֗ה וְלִפְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלִפְנֵ֥י הַנְּשִׂיאִ֖ם וְכָל־הָעֵדָ֑ה פֶּ֥תַח אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֖ד לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And they stood before Moses and before Eleazar the priest and before the leaders and all the congregation, [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting, saying,
pieces: They stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders and the whole congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said,

L.2: And they stood before Moses and before Eleazar the priest and before the leaders and all the congregation, [at the] entrance of the tent of meeting, saying,

R.2: They stood in front of Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders and the whole community at the entrance to the meeting tent. They said,

decisions.choice: at the entrance of the tent of meeting: the place where public cases were heard before the LORD
decisions.reason: The open space before the entrance of the tent was where the people gathered before the LORD and where matters too hard for the people were brought (Leviticus 8:3-4; Numbers 16:18-19). Bringing their case there put it before Moses, the priest and the people, and before the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: Eleazar the priest: Aaron's son, now high priest
decisions.reason: Aaron had died and Eleazar had taken his place (20:25-28). He stands beside Moses here as he did at the census (26:1, 63).

records.source: אָבִינוּ֮ מֵ֣ת בַּמִּדְבָּר֒ וְה֨וּא לֹא־הָיָ֜ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעֵדָ֗ה הַנּוֹעָדִ֛ים עַל־יְהוָ֖ה בַּעֲדַת־קֹ֑רַח כִּֽי־בְחֶטְא֣וֹ מֵ֔ת וּבָנִ֖ים לֹא־הָ֥יוּ לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not in [the] midst of the company, the [ones] gathered together against Yahweh in [the] company of Korah; for in his own sin he died, and sons there were not to him.
pieces: "Our father died in the wilderness. He was not one of the company who banded together against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the company of Korah. He died for his own sin, and he had no sons.

L.3: "Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not among the company that gathered together against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the company of Korah; for he died in his own sin, and he had no sons.

R.3: "Our father died in the desert. He was not one of Korah's followers, who joined together against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.

decisions.choice: not in the company of Korah: their father did not die as one of the rebels
decisions.reason: Korah and his company rose against Moses and Aaron and so against the LORD, and they died under judgment (16:1-35; 26:9-11). The daughters make plain that their father was not one of them. A rebel's family line might be thought to lose its claim, so this answers an objection before it is raised.

decisions.choice: he died in his own sin: he died for his own failings, like the rest of his generation
alternatives: he died for some sin of his own that is not named
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means that he died for his own sins as any person does, sharing the fate of the generation that refused to enter the land and so died in the wilderness (14:29-35; 26:64-65). His death was no special punishment that should cut off his family. It is not a confession of some crime.

decisions.choice: company: Korah's band, with the word used for the congregation
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the whole congregation of Israel. Used of Korah's followers, it marks them as a rival congregation (16:5).

decisions.choice: company / followers
decisions.reason: As in 16:5, Literal and Balanced say "company" for Korah's group, keeping "congregation" for Israel as a whole; Readable says "followers".

records.source: לָ֣מָּה יִגָּרַ֤ע שֵׁם־אָבִ֨ינוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ בֵּ֑ן תְּנָה־לָּ֣נוּ אֲחֻזָּ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֥י אָבִֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Why should be taken away [the] name of our father from [the] midst of his clan, because there is not to him a son? Give to us a possession in [the] midst of [the] brothers of our father.
pieces: Why should our father's name disappear from his clan because he had no son? Give us property among our father's brothers."

L.4: Why should the name of our father be taken away from the midst of his clan because he had no son? Give us a possession among the brothers of our father."

R.4: He had no son, but why should that mean our father's name is lost from his clan? Give us land of our own among our father's relatives."

decisions.choice: the name taken away: the father's family line and its land would vanish
decisions.reason: A man's "name" lived on in his descendants and in the land that carried his name in the clan's holdings. If no one inherited his share, his line would be forgotten. The same concern lies behind the law of a brother's widow (Deuteronomy 25:6) and Boaz's words in Ruth 4:10.

decisions.choice: a possession: land held as one's own by the family
decisions.reason: The word names land held by a person or family as a lasting property (Genesis 23:4, 20; Leviticus 25:10). The daughters ask for their father's share of the land to be given to them.

decisions.choice: the brothers of our father: their father's male relatives in the clan
decisions.reason: Land was shared out among the men of each clan by their fathers' houses. The daughters ask to stand among their uncles as holders of land, in their father's place.

decisions.choice: property / land of our own
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the possession is; Literal keeps "possession".

records.source: וַיַּקְרֵ֥ב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־מִשְׁפָּטָ֖ןלִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And brought near Moses their case before Yahweh.
pieces: So Moses brought their case before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.5: And Moses brought their case before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.5: So Moses took their request to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: brought their case before the LORD: asked the LORD for a ruling
decisions.reason: The word for "case" is the word for a judgment or legal ruling. When Moses met a matter the law did not yet cover, he took it to the LORD for a decision, as with the man who cursed the Name (Leviticus 24:12), those unclean at Passover (9:8) and the Sabbath breaker (15:34).

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.6: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: said ... saying: the usual way of opening the LORD's words
decisions.reason: The verb "said" followed by "saying" introduces direct speech. It is the formula used throughout Numbers.

records.source: כֵּ֗ן בְּנ֣וֹת צְלָפְחָד֮ דֹּבְרֹת֒ נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת נַחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֣י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וְהַֽעֲבַרְתָּ֛ אֶת־נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבִיהֶ֖ן לָהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: Right [the] daughters of Zelophehad [are] speaking. Surely you shall give to them a possession of inheritance in [the] midst of [the] brothers of their father, and you shall make pass over [the] inheritance of their father to them.
pieces: "The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they say. You must give them a property as an inheritance among their father's brothers, and transfer their father's inheritance to them.

L.7: "The daughters of Zelophehad are speaking right. You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance among the brothers of their father, and you shall make the inheritance of their father pass over to them.

R.7: "What the daughters of Zelophehad say is right. You must give them land to own among their father's relatives. Give them the land that would have gone to their father.

decisions.choice: right: their claim is just
decisions.reason: The word means right, true or fitting. The LORD declares that the daughters' claim is justified; the same verdict is given in 36:5 on the claim of their clan.

decisions.choice: surely you shall give: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb "give" to make the command firm and certain.

decisions.choice: a possession of inheritance: land held by right of inheritance
decisions.reason: The two words together name land received as a family's lasting share. The inheritance is the share of the land each family was to receive by lot (26:52-56).

decisions.choice: to them, their father: the first pronouns are masculine, the later ones feminine
decisions.reason: In the first half of the verse the pronouns "them" and "their" have masculine forms, in the second half feminine ones. Hebrew sometimes uses masculine forms for a group of women, and every one of these pronouns refers to the daughters. The meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: make pass over: transfer the inheritance to a new holder
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause something to pass from one to another. The father's share is not lost; it passes on to his daughters.

decisions.choice: transfer / give them the land
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "make pass over"; Balanced says "transfer" and Readable gives the sense in plain words.

records.source: וְאֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּדַבֵּ֣ר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ כִּֽי־יָמ֗וּת וּבֵן֙ אֵ֣ין ל֔וֹ וְהַֽעֲבַרְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְבִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And to [the] sons of Israel you shall speak, saying: A man, if he dies and a son there is not to him, then you shall make pass over his inheritance to his daughter.
pieces: And tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'If a man dies and has no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter.

L.8: And you shall speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, 'If a man dies and he has no son, then you shall make his inheritance pass over to his daughter.

R.8: Then tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'When a man dies and has no son, give his land to his daughter.

decisions.choice: a law for all Israel from one family's case
decisions.reason: The LORD answers the daughters' case and then makes it a general rule. Verses 8-11 set the order of heirs when a man dies: sons first, as was already the custom, then daughters, then brothers, then his father's brothers, then the nearest relative in the clan.

decisions.choice: a man: the head of a family who holds its land
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a man because land was held in the name of the male head of a family. The point of the law is that his share should pass on and stay within his clan; chapter 36 adds that daughters who inherit are to marry within their father's tribe (36:6-9).

decisions.choice: transfer / give his land
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.source: וְאִם־אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ בַּ֑ת וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם אֶת־נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְאֶחָיו׃
records.gloss: And if there is not to him a daughter, then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
pieces: If he has no daughter, you are to give his inheritance to his brothers.

L.9: And if he has no daughter, then you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.

R.9: If he has no daughter, give his land to his brothers.

decisions.choice: his brothers: the next heirs within the father's house
decisions.reason: With no child to inherit, the land goes to the dead man's brothers, so it stays within the family of his father.

decisions.choice: his land
decisions.reason: Readable says "land" for the inheritance through these verses, since the inheritance meant here is the family's share of the land.

records.source: וְאִם־אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ אַחִ֑ים וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם אֶת־נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לַאֲחֵ֥י אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And if there are not to him brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to [the] brothers of his father.
pieces: If he has no brothers, you are to give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

L.10: And if he has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to the brothers of his father.

R.10: If he has no brothers, give his land to his father's brothers.

decisions.choice: his father's brothers: his uncles, the next circle of the family
decisions.reason: The order of heirs moves outward from the dead man to his uncles, so that the land stays as close to his own line as it can.

records.source: וְאִם־אֵ֣ין אַחִים֮ לְאָבִיו֒ וּנְתַתֶּ֣ם אֶת־נַחֲלָת֗וֹ לִשְׁאֵר֞וֹ הַקָּרֹ֥ב אֵלָ֛יו מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ וְיָרַ֣שׁ אֹתָ֑הּ וְֽהָ֨יְתָ֜ה לִבְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְחֻקַּ֣ת מִשְׁפָּ֔ט כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: And if there are not brothers to his father, then you shall give his inheritance to his relative, the near [one] to him from his clan, and he shall possess it. And it shall be for [the] sons of Israel for a statute of judgment, as commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: If his father has no brothers, you are to give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan, and he will take possession of it. This is to be a legal statute for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}},'" just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses.

L.11: And if his father has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his relative who is nearest to him from his clan, and he shall possess it. And it shall be for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel a statute of judgment,'" just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses.

R.11: If his father has no brothers, give his land to his closest relative in his clan. That relative will own it. This is a law for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to follow.'" This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: his relative, the nearest to him: his closest kin by blood
decisions.reason: The word for "relative" means one's own flesh, a blood relation (Leviticus 18:6; 25:49). The nearest kinsman of the clan inherits, so the land never leaves the clan.

decisions.choice: a statute of judgment: a fixed rule of law
decisions.reason: "Statute" is a fixed, lasting law and "judgment" a legal ruling. Together they mark this as a standing rule of law for Israel, to be followed in deciding such cases. The phrase is used again in 35:29.

decisions.choice: as the LORD commanded Moses: the narrator's closing words, after the LORD's speech ends
decisions.reason: The LORD's words end with the statute. The last clause is the narrator's formula, telling the reader that this law came from the LORD through Moses. It could also be read as the last words of the speech, but it is the narrator's usual way of closing a law given through Moses (compare verse 22 and 31:31). The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: a statute of judgment / a legal statute / a law
decisions.reason: Literal keeps both words; Balanced joins them as "a legal statute", and Readable says "a law".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה עֲלֵ֛ה אֶל־הַ֥ר הָעֲבָרִ֖ים הַזֶּ֑ה וּרְאֵה֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, Go up to mountain the Abarim the this, and see the land that I have given to [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Climb this mountain in the Abarim range and look out over the land I have given to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.12: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go up to this mountain of the Abarim and see the land that I have given to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.12: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Climb up onto this mountain in the Abarim hills. Look out over the land I have given to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: the mountain of the Abarim: the heights east of the Jordan facing the land
decisions.reason: The name means "the regions across", the hills on the eastern side of the Dead Sea and the Jordan, opposite Jericho, where Israel was camped (22:1; 33:47-48). Deuteronomy 32:49 and 34:1 name the peak Moses climbed as Mount Nebo in this range.

decisions.choice: I have given: the gift is already settled
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks of the land as already given, though Israel has not yet entered it. The gift is certain because he has decided it (20:12).

decisions.choice: see the land: Moses may see it but not enter it
decisions.reason: Moses is allowed to see the land from far off, as the next verses explain, because he will not go into it (20:12; Deuteronomy 3:23-27; 34:1-4).

decisions.choice: this mountain in the Abarim range / hills
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "range" or "hills" to show that Abarim names a line of heights, not one mountain.

records.heading: Joshua appointed to succeed Moses

records.source: וְרָאִ֣יתָה אֹתָ֔הּ וְנֶאֱסַפְתָּ֥ אֶל־עַמֶּ֖יךָ גַּם־אָ֑תָּה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶאֱסַ֖ף אַהֲרֹ֥ן אָחִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And you will see it, and you will be gathered to your people, also you, as was gathered Aaron your brother,
pieces: When you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was,

L.13: And you shall see it, and you shall be gathered to your people, you also, just as Aaron your brother was gathered,

R.13: After you have seen it, you will die and join your people who died before you, just as your brother Aaron did.

decisions.choice: be gathered to your people: die and join one's ancestors
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the death of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Aaron (Genesis 25:8; 35:29; 49:33; Numbers 20:24, 26). It speaks of death as going to be with those of one's family who died before.

decisions.choice: as Aaron your brother was gathered: Aaron's death on Mount Hor
decisions.reason: Aaron had gone up Mount Hor and died there, after his priestly clothes were put on Eleazar (20:22-29). Moses is told that his own death will come in the same way, on a mountain, and that a successor must be named.

decisions.choice: you will die and join your people who died before you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of being gathered to one's people means. Literal and Balanced keep the picture.

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ מְרִיתֶ֨ם פִּ֜י בְּמִדְבַּר־צִ֗ן בִּמְרִיבַת֙ הָֽעֵדָ֔ה לְהַקְדִּישֵׁ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם לְעֵינֵיהֶ֑ם הֵ֛ם מֵֽי־מְרִיבַ֥ת קָדֵ֖שׁ מִדְבַּר־צִֽן׃פ
records.gloss: because you rebelled [against] my mouth in [the] wilderness of Zin, in [the] quarreling of the congregation, to treat as holy me at the waters before their eyes. They [are the] waters of Meribah [of] Kadesh, [in the] wilderness of Zin.
pieces: for when the congregation quarreled in the wilderness of Zin, you rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} command to show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness before their eyes at the waters." (These were the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.)

L.14: because you rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth in the wilderness of Zin, in the quarreling of the congregation, to treat {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as holy at the waters before their eyes." (These [are the] waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)

R.14: This is because you and Aaron went against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} command in the Zin Desert. When the people quarreled there, you did not show them that I am holy at the water." (This was at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the Zin Desert.)

decisions.choice: you rebelled: "you" is plural, Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. The LORD speaks to Moses about what he and Aaron did together at Meribah, as in 20:12 and 20:24, where Aaron's death was announced for the same reason.

decisions.choice: rebelled against my command to treat me as holy: the failure at the waters of Meribah
decisions.reason: In 20:1-13 the LORD told Moses to speak to the rock before the people's eyes, but Moses struck it twice and spoke as if he and Aaron were bringing out the water. The LORD said they had not trusted him or shown his holiness before the people (20:12). The command they went against was the command that would have shown the LORD as holy. "Mouth" here means the spoken command.

decisions.choice: Meribah of Kadesh: "quarreling" at Kadesh
decisions.reason: Meribah means "quarreling" and is the same word used just before for the congregation's quarrel. Kadesh comes from the root for "holy", the word in "treat me as holy", so the place names echo what happened there (20:13). The name Meribah was also given to a place near Rephidim (Exodus 17:7), so "of Kadesh" marks which one is meant.

decisions.choice: These are the waters of Meribah: a note to the reader
decisions.reason: The last sentence explains the place named. It reads like the narrator's note, as at 20:13, and is set apart here. It can also be read as the end of the LORD's words, which would not change the meaning.

decisions.choice: command
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "command" for "mouth", which here means what the LORD said. Literal keeps "mouth".

decisions.choice: you and Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names Aaron because English "you" does not show the plural, following meaning decision m1.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Moses to Yahweh, saying,
pieces: Moses said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

L.15: And Moses spoke to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying,

decisions.choice: Moses answers with a prayer for the people
decisions.reason: Moses does not plead for himself, as he did at another time (Deuteronomy 3:23-26). His concern is that the people should have a leader after him.

records.source: יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָרוּחֹ֖ת לְכָל־בָּשָׂ֑ר אִ֖ישׁ עַל־הָעֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: Let appoint Yahweh, God of the spirits of all flesh, a man over the congregation,
pieces: "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the spirits of all humankind, appoint a man over the congregation,

L.16: "Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,

R.16: "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God who gives life and breath to every person, choose a man to lead the community.

decisions.choice: the God of the spirits of all flesh: the God who gives every human being life
decisions.reason: The title was first used by Moses and Aaron in 16:22. "Flesh" means living humankind and "spirit" the breath of life God gives (Genesis 2:7; 6:17). Because God gives each person life and knows each one, he can choose the right leader.

decisions.choice: appoint: put someone in charge over others
decisions.reason: The verb has a wide range: to count and muster, as in the census (1:3; 26:2), or to put someone in charge, as here and in 3:10. With "over" it means to set a man in authority over the people.

decisions.choice: let the LORD appoint: a request, not a command
decisions.reason: The verb form expresses a wish addressed respectfully to the LORD in the third person, a polite form of prayer.

decisions.choice: all humankind
decisions.reason: As in 16:22, Balanced says "all humankind" for "all flesh", and Readable turns the title into a statement of what it means.

records.source: אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵ֣א לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יָבֹא֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹצִיאֵ֖ם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר יְבִיאֵ֑ם וְלֹ֤א תִהְיֶה֙ עֲדַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כַּצֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־לָהֶ֖ם רֹעֶֽה׃
records.gloss: who will go out before them and who will come in before them, and who will lead them out and who will bring them in, and not will be [the] congregation of Yahweh like sheep that there is not to them a shepherd.
pieces: someone who will go out ahead of them and come in ahead of them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not be like sheep with no shepherd."

L.17: who will go out before them and who will come in before them, and who will lead them out and who will bring them in, so that the congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not be like sheep that have no shepherd."

R.17: He must go ahead of them and lead them wherever they go and whenever they come back. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people will not be like sheep with no shepherd to care for them."

decisions.choice: go out and come in: lead the people in all their life, especially in war
decisions.reason: To "go out and come in" before a people is to lead them in all they do, and very often it means leading them out to battle and home again (Joshua 14:11; 1 Samuel 18:13, 16; 2 Samuel 5:2). The leader goes ahead of them himself, and he also leads them out and brings them back.

decisions.choice: like sheep that have no shepherd: a people with no one to guide and protect them
decisions.reason: A shepherd led his flock to food and water and kept it from harm. Leaders were often pictured as shepherds, and a people without a ruler as scattered sheep (1 Kings 22:17; Ezekiel 34:5).

decisions.choice: with no shepherd to care for them
decisions.reason: Readable adds what a shepherd does, to make the picture clear; Literal and Balanced keep the bare picture. Readable also explains "go out and come in" in plain words, following meaning decision m1.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה קַח־לְךָ֙ אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־נ֔וּן אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־ר֣וּחַ בּ֑וֹ וְסָמַכְתָּ֥ אֶת־יָדְךָ֖ עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, Take for yourself Joshua son of Nun, a man who spirit [is] in him, and lay your hand on him,
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the spirit in him, and lay your hand on him,

L.18: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Take for yourself Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom [is] spirit, and lay your hand on him,

R.18: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun. He is a man with the spirit in him. Lay your hand on him.

decisions.choice: a man in whom is spirit: a man given the spirit to lead
alternatives: a man in whom is the Spirit (of God)
a man with the spirit of wisdom and courage
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "spirit" with no article and no "of God". It may mean the LORD's Spirit, which rested on the elders in 11:17, 25-29 and was seen in Joseph (Genesis 41:38). It may instead mean the gifts of mind and courage a leader needs; Deuteronomy 34:9 calls Joshua "full of the spirit of wisdom". Either way Joshua is already fit for the task before hands are laid on him.

decisions.choice: lay your hand on him: a sign that he is set apart for his task
decisions.reason: Laying a hand on someone or something marked it out and joined it to the one acting, in offerings (Leviticus 1:4) and in setting the Levites apart (8:10). Here it shows that Joshua is chosen and gives him a share in Moses' authority (verse 20; Deuteronomy 34:9). Verse 23 says Moses laid both hands on him.

decisions.choice: Joshua son of Nun: Moses' assistant
decisions.reason: Joshua had served Moses from his youth (11:28), led Israel in battle (Exodus 17:9-13), and was one of the two spies who trusted the LORD (14:6-9, 30).

decisions.choice: Take Joshua / the spirit
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out "for yourself", which in Hebrew goes naturally with "take" and adds nothing in English. They write "the spirit" with a small letter, which keeps both readings of meaning decision m1 open.

records.source: וְהַֽעֲמַדְתָּ֣ אֹת֗וֹ לִפְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָּל־הָעֵדָ֑ה וְצִוִּיתָ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: and you shall make stand him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation, and you shall commission him before their eyes,
pieces: have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight,

L.19: and you shall make him stand before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation, and you shall commission him before their eyes,

R.19: Have him stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the whole community. Then give him his charge while they all watch.

decisions.choice: commission: give him his charge as leader
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual word for "command". Said of a person, it means to give him his orders and appoint him to a task. Deuteronomy 3:28 and 31:7-8, 23 give the words of this charge to Joshua: be strong and courageous, for he will bring Israel into the land.

decisions.choice: before their eyes: in public, so that all would know he was the leader
decisions.reason: The appointment is made before the priest and the whole congregation, so that no one could later question Joshua's right to lead, as Korah questioned Moses (16:3).

decisions.choice: give him his charge
decisions.reason: Readable says what commissioning is in plainer words.

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֥ה מֵהֽוֹדְךָ֖ עָלָ֑יו לְמַ֣עַן יִשְׁמְע֔וּ כָּל־עֲדַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: and you shall put from your majesty on him, so that will listen all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: and give him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will obey him.

L.20: and you shall put some of your majesty on him, so that all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel will listen.

R.20: Share some of your authority with him. Then the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} will obey him.

decisions.choice: majesty: the honor and authority of a leader
decisions.reason: The word means splendor or majesty, often the dignity of a king (Psalm 21:6; 1 Chronicles 29:25). Here it is the standing and authority Moses had among the people, which Joshua is to share.

decisions.choice: some of your majesty: a share, not all of it
decisions.reason: The word "from" marks a part. Joshua receives a share of Moses' authority, enough for the people to follow him, while Moses' place as the one the LORD spoke with face to face stays his own (12:6-8; Deuteronomy 34:10).

decisions.choice: listen: heed and obey
decisions.reason: The verb "hear" often means to listen and do what is said. The people are to follow Joshua as they followed Moses (Deuteronomy 34:9; Joshua 1:16-17).

decisions.choice: authority / obey him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "authority" for the word Literal gives as "majesty", and "obey him" for "listen", the sense in this verse.

records.source: וְלִפְנֵ֨י אֶלְעָזָ֤ר הַכֹּהֵן֙ יַעֲמֹ֔ד וְשָׁ֥אַל ל֛וֹ בְּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט הָאוּרִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה עַל־פִּ֨יו יֵצְא֜וּ וְעַל־פִּ֣יו יָבֹ֗אוּ ה֛וּא וְכָל־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אִתּ֖וֹ וְכָל־הָעֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And before Eleazar the priest he shall stand, and he shall inquire for him by [the] judgment of the Urim before Yahweh; at his mouth they shall go out and at his mouth they shall come in, he and all [the] sons of Israel with him, and all the congregation.
pieces: He is to stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek decisions for him before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by means of the Urim. At his word they will go out, and at his word they will come in, Joshua and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} with him, the whole congregation."

L.21: And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and he shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. At his mouth they shall go out and at his mouth they shall come in, he and all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel with him, and all the congregation."

R.21: Joshua must go to Eleazar the priest when he needs to know what to do. Eleazar will use the Urim to ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has decided. At the word given through Eleazar, Joshua and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, the whole community, will set out and will come back."

decisions.choice: before Eleazar he shall stand: Joshua will seek the LORD's will through the priest
decisions.reason: Moses spoke with the LORD face to face (12:8; Exodus 33:11). Joshua will not; he will learn the LORD's will through the high priest. Leadership after Moses is shared between the leader and the priest.

decisions.choice: the judgment of the Urim: a decision sought from the LORD with the sacred lots
decisions.reason: The Urim, with the Thummim, were kept in the high priest's breastpiece and used to ask the LORD for a decision (Exodus 28:30; 1 Samuel 28:6). Only the Urim is named here, standing for both. How they were used is not told; they probably gave a yes or no answer. The name is left untranslated, as in Exodus 28:30.

decisions.choice: at his mouth: at the word Eleazar gives from the LORD
decisions.reason: "His" most likely refers to Eleazar, who gives the answer from the LORD; the next words make Joshua and the people the ones who go out at that word. It could also refer to the LORD, whose decision Eleazar seeks. In either case the people move at the LORD's word given through the priest.

decisions.choice: go out and come in: set out on campaigns and journeys and return
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, the pair covers all the people's ventures, especially going out to war.

decisions.choice: Joshua
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Joshua where the Hebrew says "he", since the sentence has already spoken of Eleazar and "he" could be misread. Readable also says "at the word given through Eleazar", which fits both readings of meaning decision m3, and adds "when he needs to know what to do" to say why Joshua stands before the priest.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ וַיַּֽעֲמִדֵ֨הוּ֙ לִפְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלִפְנֵ֖י כָּל־הָעֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And did Moses as commanded Yahweh him; and he took Joshua and made stand him before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation,
pieces: Moses did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation,

L.22: And Moses did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him, and he took Joshua and made him stand before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation,

R.22: Moses did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told him. He brought Joshua and had him stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the whole community.

decisions.choice: Moses did as the LORD commanded: his last act of leadership in Numbers is obedience
decisions.reason: Moses had been told that he went against the LORD's command at Meribah (verse 14). Here he does exactly what he is told, in front of all the people.

records.source: וַיִּסְמֹ֧ךְ אֶת־יָדָ֛יו עָלָ֖יו וַיְצַוֵּ֑הוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as had spoken Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.
pieces: and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had directed through Moses.

L.23: and he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken by the hand of Moses.

R.23: Then Moses laid his hands on Joshua and gave him his charge, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through Moses.

decisions.choice: his hands: both hands, where verse 18 says "hand"
decisions.reason: The LORD told Moses to lay his hand on Joshua (verse 18), and Moses lays both hands on him. The singular in verse 18 names the act, and the meaning is the same. Deuteronomy 34:9 also says "his hands".

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" someone means through that person as the LORD's agent. It is the usual way Numbers speaks of the LORD's commands given through Moses (4:37; 9:23; 15:23).

decisions.choice: through Moses
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "by the hand of"; Literal keeps the picture. Readable names Moses and Joshua for clarity.
